title: Dashboard
impl: Every tile is a saved query against existing indexes — no separate metrics store.
Needs-attention rows are derived facts, not alerts: no thresholds, no notifications.
Collection chart reads job history, bucketed hourly server-side.
Cluster risk order is fixed: failing collection, then drift, then cert expiry.
Coverage strip is the freshness histogram of the snapshot table, not a separate metric.

title: Trace
impl: Graph is a static DAG (≤40 nodes) — plain SVG/flex layout, no physics engine.
Rules fired groups by hop; a hop band folds its rules away so a long path stays readable. Fold state is client-side only.
Rules table = server-paged; row select drives provenance panel via hop+rule id.
Provenance renders stored snapshot bytes verbatim; highlight = byte range.
State per row comes from the trace engine only — never recomputed client-side.

title: Trace › Probe
impl: One request per click, never scheduled; every probe row is audit-logged.
Log correlation = bounded tail + grep for the probe id on each hop node.
Hops without the needed log field stay INFERRED — no heuristic upgrade.
State changes write to the trace record, not to the node's snapshot.

title: Trace › Probe history
impl: Probe history is a sub-route of Trace, not a top-level section.
Every probe row is the audit record itself — immutable, retention-bound.
State changes are stored on the trace record they belong to, and read out inside the expanded row — no right-hand preview card.

title: Rule lookup
impl: Two-field form is the default entry; the parsed query grammar sits behind “Advanced”.
Facet counts from indexed aggregations, capped at top 10.
Server-side keyset pagination; group headers are collapsed by default beyond page 1.
Plain-language text is templated per directive type — a fixed table, not NLP.
SHADOWED = vendor precedence says an earlier rule wins; computed at index time.
Nodes with byte-identical rule sets collapse into one row with a count.

title: Config search
impl: Index covers the current snapshot per node only — older snapshots are file-browsable.
Substring / regex both supported; regex queries are timeboxed server-side.
Line context comes from the stored file blob, offset-addressed.
Results paginate by file, not by match, to keep response size bounded.

title: Sites
impl: Site = distinct server_name/vhost/frontend hostname, aggregated fleet-wide at index time.
Variant = hash of the normalised route+upstream set for that hostname on each node.
Aliases fold into the primary row; the row’s expansion lists them.
Variant comparison expands under the hostname it belongs to — no separate preview panel to re-anchor on.
Same records as before — this is a different primary key, not a new collector.

title: Site detail
impl: One hostname across the fleet; every count on this page is fleet-wide, not per node.
Variant selector rewrites the routes table only — node list always shows all variants.
Routes are the plain-English projection; raw directives stay in Node › Config files.
Rows link down to the node that serves them, never to a per-process page.

title: Nodes
impl: One tree, three levels: cluster band → node row → process row. Clusters are reconciled from collected configuration (never created), so the band is a grouping of what was found, not an object anyone edits — beyond renaming it.
A node lands under the one cluster its processes share; a node whose processes sit in different clusters, or in none, groups under “— no cluster”.
Expand-in-place fetches that node's processes only (lazy, one request per open node).
Cluster-band actions are the whole of cluster administration: rename, clear baseline, open the drift report.
“Listeners” is a denormalised summary column written at collection time.

title: Node detail
impl: Node is the addressable unit; the process picker appears only when a node runs >1.
With one process the picker renders as static text — no extra click, no extra page.
Every site row carries its fleet count, so the node view links back up to Sites.
Replaces the separate per-process list and its scoped tabs.

title: Node › Routes
impl: No directive names in this view — every line is generated from the parsed object.
Plain wording is a fixed template per action type (rewrite, proxy, header, auth, cache, limit).
“Test a path” resolves against the indexed route set for this site — no request is sent.
A “Wording: exact directives” toggle exists for users who want the vendor terms back.
Shadowed routes are listed as “never reached” with the reason, not as an error.

title: Node › Upstreams
impl: Member → Node mapping is an inventory join on IP:port, done at index time.
DNS-named members are stored as names; nagipath does not resolve them itself.
PARTIAL means at least one member could not be mapped — never guessed.
Members and the resolution summary expand under their pool; only the open pool’s members are fetched.

title: Node › Certificates
impl: This view is the fleet certificate index filtered to one node.
File paths and modes come from stat on the node; contents are not read.
Chain length is counted from the served PEM, leaf excluded.
SANs, issuer and the fleet-wide binding list expand under the binding row — no right-hand preview.

title: Node › Config files
impl: This view is the only place raw directives appear; it never interprets them.
Tree is the include graph, not the filesystem — inactive files are marked, not hidden.
Follow-include arrows navigate to the target file at the right line.
Per-file history replaces the global Snapshots page; diffs are line-level here, object-level in Routes.
“What does this do?” jumps the highlighted block into the Routes view.

title: Drift
impl: Entry point is a work queue: nodes with unreviewed divergences first.
Clusters without a declared baseline are excluded and say so, not silently empty.
Counts come from the last diff job, not recomputed on page load.

title: Drift review
impl: Diff is over raw file text from the two snapshots — no parsing, no object model.
File list, +/− counts, per-file Viewed and hunk collapse follow the pull-request convention.
Whitespace and comment-only changes are filtered by a diff option, not by interpretation.
Ignore rules are stored as file + hunk hash, scoped to cluster or fleet, and survive re-diffs.
“Next node” walks the drift queue keeping scroll and view options.

title: Certificates
impl: Metadata only — cert and key files are never fetched or stored.
Deduped by SHA-256; bindings are (node, site, listener) tuples.
SANs and the binding list expand under the fingerprint they describe — one row open at a time, fetched on expand.
HAProxy combined PEM: parse leaf only, ignore trailing key block.
Expiry buckets computed server-side so counts match the filter exactly.

title: Certificate detail
impl: One row per fingerprint; this page is every place that fingerprint is served.
Chain completeness comes from the files present on each node, not from a live handshake.
File rows are stat output — nagipath never reads private keys or cert bodies.
“Find replacements” searches the index for a newer cert covering the same SAN set.

title: Settings
impl: Settings sub-nav is a plain routed list — one panel per section.
Role scope is a cluster glob checked server-side on every request.
Retention writes a background prune job; no destructive immediate delete.

title: Settings › Credentials
impl: Secrets are write-only: enter once, never rendered back to any role.
Assignment is by cluster glob; per-node overrides live on the node record.
Test runs a connect + sudo -n check only — it collects nothing.
The detail and the last test result expand under the credential row; there is no separate preview card.

title: Settings › Host keys
impl: Pending keys block collection rather than silently trusting the host.
A changed key is never auto-approved — it is a distinct state with the old value kept.
Approvals are audited with the approving user and the fingerprint at that moment.

A ticked key expands in place: recorded vs presented fingerprint under the row it belongs to, not in a preview card. Policy stays a panel — it is a fixed statement about the install, not a row detail.

title: Settings › Collection defaults
impl: Schedules resolve top-down; a node collected by an earlier rule is skipped by later ones.
Per-schedule overrides shadow these defaults for that target only.
Coverage check reports nodes matched by no schedule before you save.

title: Settings › Collection jobs
impl: Was the top-level “Collections” section — it is operational history, so it lives in Settings.
Queued jobs with a global concurrency cap; no agent runs on the nodes.
Degraded is a first-class outcome: snapshot stored, source of truth downgraded.
The job log expands under its own run — a right-hand log pane makes you re-check which row you were reading.

title: Settings › Master key
impl: Secrets are wrapped, not stored: losing the KMS key makes credentials unrecoverable by design.
Sealed state blocks collection and probes but leaves the index readable.
Rotation is online — old key versions are kept until every record is re-wrapped.

title: Settings › Retention
impl: Prune is a background job — nothing is deleted at the moment you save.
Audit retention cannot be set below 365 days by any role.
Exceptions are evaluated per record, so counts here always reconcile with the class totals.

title: Settings › API keys
impl: Secret is displayed once; only the prefix is stored for identification.
Scope is a route allow-list intersected with the owner’s cluster scope.
Denied calls are kept in the audit log with the reason, not silently dropped.
Scope and recent calls expand under the key they belong to; the “New key” form is the only separate panel, and it is a form, not a preview.

title: Settings › Audit log
impl: Append-only store; no role can edit or delete an event.
Every settings mutation writes before/after values, not just the action name.
The full record expands under its own event row — nothing is pre-selected, so arriving on the page shows the log, not one arbitrary event.
Denied API calls and failed logins are events too — absence of an event is meaningful.

title: Nodes › Import inventory
impl: Step 1 (Paste): the paste form is unchanged — one host per line or an Ansible INI/YAML inventory, credential picked from stored credentials, no network or CIDR scanning ever. Its button reads “Parse and continue”, not “Import” — it only parses; nothing is written yet. A refused line is reported with its line number and reason and does not block the rest.

Step 2 (Test): each parsed node gets one real SSH connection attempt with the chosen credential — the only network traffic nagipath ever originates toward a pasted host, run once here rather than deferred to the first scheduled collection. Rows test in parallel, capped the same as a collection run.

An unknown or changed host key blocks that row’s connection and expands it in place — same layout and actions as Settings / Host keys — so approval happens without leaving the import. Approving retests only that row; rejecting excludes the node from step 3 without discarding the rest of the import.
“Continue to confirm” stays disabled while any row is still testing. A node stuck FAILED or BLOCKED isn’t forced — step 3 lets it through as “not collected yet” or drops it, the operator’s call.

Step 3 (Confirm): one summary of ready vs. excluded nodes, a “Start collection now” toggle (default on) alongside Import, and a plain Import writes the node rows only. A retry from Step 2 never re-asks for the pasted text — parsed rows stay in memory across all three steps.

title: Snapshots
impl: Every provenance link in the product lands in this store; the list is the way back out of it.
Paging is a cursor, not an offset — the window keeps filling while you read it.
CHANGED means the captured bytes differ from the previous snapshot of the same instance.
No sidebar row: Snapshots is reached from a node or a provenance link, so the crumb names Inventory and no nav item is active.

title: Snapshot › File
impl: The far end of every provenance link: ?b=<block id> highlights the block and scrolls it into view.
Bytes are served from the snapshot, never re-read from the node — the file may have changed since.
No syntax service: highlighting is the anchored range only, so it cannot disagree with what was collected.

title: Settings › License
impl: Status is evaluated on read, not cached — an expired license reports itself the moment it expires.
Over the node ceiling degrades to a warning; nagipath never stops collecting or locks the UI.
A viewer can read status; only an admin sees the install form.
Installing replaces the stored license outright; the previous one is recorded in the audit log.

title: Settings › System
impl: Every value is read live from the process and the database file — nothing is cached or configured here.
Migrations applied vs. expected is the one field that can say the binary and the database disagree.
The bundle is a text/plain attachment, deliberately not JSON, so it can be pasted into a ticket.
The redaction list is enforced when the bundle is built, not filtered afterwards.

title: Change password
impl: Inside the normal chrome: there is a session, so the sidebar and header are drawn as usual.
While a temporary password is set, every other page redirects here and the current-password field is replaced by a warning callout.
No sidebar row and no Settings rail — this is reached from the avatar menu, so the crumb is the page itself.

title: Sign in
impl: No header, no sidebar: there is no session yet to draw either from.
?next= is followed only when it is a local path, so a login link cannot bounce you off-host.
One error string for a bad username and a bad password — the form never says which was wrong.
If the database has no users at all, this redirects to first-run setup instead.

title: First-run setup
impl: Reachable only while the database has no users; once one exists this redirects to Sign in.
The create call refuses a second administrator on its own — the redirect is convenience, not the guard.
The master key is generated on first start, not here; this screen only creates the operator account.
